evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: the constructor declares `@InjectRepository(CourseEntity) private readonly courseRepository: Repository<CourseEntity>`, but no method ever reads `this.courseRepository`.
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: in `enrol`, `const courseRepository = getRepository(CourseEntity);` uses TypeORM's global getRepository imported from 'typeorm'.
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: `courseRepository.findOne({ where: { id: courseId } })` and `courseRepository.save(entity)` go through the global repository, not the injected one.
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: enrolment persistence uses the injected `this.enrolmentRepository`, so the two entities are reached in two different ways.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: EnrolmentsService injects `courseRepository: Repository<CourseEntity>` through `@InjectRepository(CourseEntity)` but never uses it. In `enrol` it calls TypeORM's global `getRepository(CourseEntity)` and does its `findOne` and `save` calls for courses through that local variable, so it gets to persistence around the repository the module injects. The local `courseRepository` also hides the injected field of the same name, which makes the bypass easy to miss. This is the repo-bypass case the rubric names, so the unit fails. The direct-ORM and repo-bypass candidate flags are both confirmed. The broad-responsibility flag is not supported: enrolling and withdrawing are one concern. The inline email check (`includes('@')`) might be duplicated elsewhere, but no second copy appears in the source I was given, so I don't count it.

This goes around the CourseEntity repository injected in the constructor (`this.courseRepository`), which is never used. The local variable also hides the injected field of the same name.
